LESSON: WRITING 5.3.1 CREATIVE WRITING: CREATIVE LANGUAGE

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.3: Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language, part of Strand 5 in Grade 6 INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES.

Key inquiry question: How do we develop good handwriting?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. write texts based on the theme neatly and legibly for effective communication,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate creativity and handwriting in effective communication.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency,

   Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. write texts based on the theme neatly and legibly for effective communication,

   Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate creativity and handwriting in effective communication.

   Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. discuss the use of creative language in writing: proverbs, metaphors, saying and similes,

2. read sample compositions online and offline to identify creative language,

3. team up to create a collection of proverbs, similes, sayings and metaphors from texts,

4. write a creative composition neatly and legibly,

5. participate in a writing contest to practice creativity and handwriting.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. discuss the use of creative language in writing: proverbs, metaphors, saying and similes,
2. read sample compositions online and offline to identify creative language,
3. team up to create a collection of proverbs, similes, sayings and metaphors from texts,
4. write a creative composition neatly and legibly,
5. participate in a writing contest to practice creativity and handwriting.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 5.3.1 Creative Writing: Creative language together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Creativity and Imagination: This is developed as the learner exchanges ideas that inspire creativity when composing own

compositions neatly and in good handwriting.

● Digital Literacy: This is cultivated as the learner interacts with technology to read sample compositions online and offline

to identify creative language.

30

Values:
● Unity: This is cultivated as the learner teams up to create a collection of proverbs, similes, sayings and metaphors from

texts.

● Responsibility: This is developed as the learner takes own initiative to participate in a writing contest to practice creativity

and handwriting.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Sustainable development: This is enhanced as learners get exposed to content on farming for crop production.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate the concept of good handwriting and creative language to their writing activities in English.

31

ambulance, syringe, medicine, bandage, food

SECTION 6: SUMMARY

Main points to remember:

1. identify aspects of creative language in texts based on the theme for fluency,
2. write texts based on the theme neatly and legibly for effective communication,
3. appreciate creativity and handwriting in effective communication.

Remember the key question: How do we develop good handwriting?
